items.title: Three environments with managed data stores
items.description_md: As a TaskFlow engineer, I want separate dev, stg and prod environments, each with its own database and cache, so that features can be built, verified and released safely and the whole platform stays inside the monthly infrastructure budget. **Why this priority**: Every other feature in the backlog needs a place to run and a database and cache to use; nothing can be released without it. **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by bringing up each environment, checking that the API, web app and worker workloads start, that the database and cache accept connections from the workloads only, and that the cost report for all three environments is under the budget. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the infrastructure definitions for dev, stg and prod, **When** an environment is created, **Then** it is isolated from the other two (own cluster namespace or cluster, own database, own cache) and runs in the AWS us-east-1 region. 2. **Given** an environment, **When** the API, web and worker workloads are scheduled, **Then** the database and cache are reachable from those workloads and are not reachable from the public internet. 3. **Given** all three environments are running, **When** the monthly cost is reviewed, **Then** the forecast total is at most USD 2,500 across all environments. 4. **Given** the production environment, **When** one workload instance fails, **Then** at least one other instance of the API and web app keeps serving traffic. ---

user_story.i_want: separate dev, stg and prod environments, each with its own database and cache
user_story.so_that: features can be built, verified and released safely and the whole platform stays inside the monthly infrastructure budget

items.title: CI/CD for api, web and worker
items.description_md: As a TaskFlow engineer, I want every change to be built, tested and deployed automatically through the environments so that releases are repeatable and a broken change never reaches production unnoticed. **Why this priority**: Without a pipeline no feature can reach pilot customers by the mid-December 2026 beta, and uncontrolled releases threaten the availability target. **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by merging a trivial change in each repository and watching it build, pass tests, deploy to dev, promote to stg, and (after approval) to prod, then rolling back to the previous version. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a pull request in the api or web repository, **When** it is opened or updated, **Then** unit and integration tests run and the pull request cannot be merged while they fail. 2. **Given** a change merged to the main branch, **When** the pipeline runs, **Then** one image is built for the api and the worker (same repository and image, different start command) and a build of the web app is produced, and both are deployed to dev automatically. 3. **Given** a version running in stg that passed its checks, **When** an engineer approves promotion, **Then** the same build artifact is deployed to prod without being rebuilt. 4. **Given** a deployment to prod whose health check fails, **When** the rollout does not become healthy, **Then** the previous version keeps serving traffic and the failed deployment is reported. 5. **Given** the pipeline definitions, **When** they are reviewed, **Then** they contain no secret values. ---

user_story.so_that: releases are repeatable and a broken change never reaches production unnoticed

items.title: Secrets delivered without being stored in Git
items.description_md: As a TaskFlow engineer, I want the database URL, Redis URL and email provider key to be stored in AWS Secrets Manager and delivered to the workloads automatically so that no secret ever appears in Git and confidential task data stays protected. **Why this priority**: Workloads cannot start without their connection settings, and the constitution forbids secrets in code or configuration files. **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by creating a secret in an environment's Secrets Manager, observing it appear as an environment variable in the workload, rotating it, and scanning all repositories for secret values. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the three secrets (database URL, Redis URL, email provider key) in an environment's Secrets Manager, **When** a workload starts, **Then** each secret is available to it as an environment variable. 2. **Given** a secret value changes in Secrets Manager, **When** the synchronisation interval passes and workloads are restarted, **Then** they use the new value without any change in Git. 3. **Given** any of the repositories, **When** a secret scan runs in CI, **Then** it finds no secret values and fails the build if it finds one. 4. **Given** the dev, stg and prod environments, **When** their secrets are compared, **Then** each environment only has access to its own secrets. ---

items.title: Users, boards and board membership data foundation
items.description_md: As a TaskFlow developer, I want the users, boards and board membership data structures and a versioned migration process in place so that every later feature stores its data on the same, reviewed foundation. **Why this priority**: Membership is what the confidentiality rule (NFR-3) is based on, and all feature teams add their own migrations on top of this base. **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by applying all migrations to an empty database, creating users, a board and memberships, and verifying uniqueness and referential rules, then rolling the migration back and forward again. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an empty database, **When** migrations are applied, **Then** users, boards and board memberships exist and the migration history records the version. 2. **Given** a user who is already a member of a board, **When** the same membership is created again, **Then** it is rejected and no duplicate exists. 3. **Given** a board with members, **When** a user is added as a member, **Then** the membership is stored with the user, the board and the member's role (owner or member). 4. **Given** a new feature needs a table, **When** a developer adds a migration, **Then** the migration runs in CI against a clean database and after the previous release's schema. ---

user_story.so_that: every later feature stores its data on the same, reviewed foundation

items.title: Authentication
items.description_md: As a team member, I want to sign in so that the platform knows who I am and every request I make is tied to my identity. **Why this priority**: Authorisation (US6) is impossible without a known caller identity. **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by signing in with valid and invalid credentials and calling an authenticated endpoint with a valid, an expired and a missing credential. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a registered user, **When** they sign in with correct credentials, **Then** they receive a credential (bearer token) that identifies them on later requests. 2. **Given** a user with wrong credentials, **When** they try to sign in, **Then** access is refused with a generic message that does not reveal whether the account exists. 3. **Given** a request to a protected endpoint with no, malformed or expired credential, **When** it is processed, **Then** it is refused as unauthenticated and no data is returned. 4. **Given** repeated failed sign-in attempts for one account, **When** the limit is exceeded, **Then** further attempts are temporarily refused. 5. **Given** a signed-in user, **When** they ask who they are, **Then** the system returns their own profile only. ---

items.title: Board-member authorisation on every board-scoped endpoint
items.description_md: As a team member, I want only the members of a board to be able to see or change anything on it so that my team's task data stays confidential. **Why this priority**: This is the core of the security and privacy requirement (NFR-3); all later task, search, comment, report and export endpoints must reuse it. **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested with two boards and two users, each a member of only one: every board-scoped endpoint must answer the non-member with a refusal and reveal nothing, while the member is served. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a board and a user who is not a member, **When** the user requests the board or anything under it, **Then** the system refuses and returns no board or task data; the response is indistinguishable from a board that does not exist. 2. **Given** a board member, **When** they request the board, **Then** they are served. 3. **Given** a user removed from a board, **When** they make the next request, **Then** they no longer have access, including to cached data. 4. **Given** a new board-scoped endpoint added by any feature, **When** it is built, **Then** it uses the shared membership check, and an automated test fails if a registered board-scoped route does not enforce it. 5. **Given** a list or search spanning several boards, **When** a user requests it, **Then** only data from boards where they are a member is included. 6. **Given** any refused access, **When** it happens, **Then** an audit-style log entry records the user, the board and the time, without task content. ---

user_story.so_that: my team's task data stays confidential

items.title: Availability monitoring and service-level alerting
items.description_md: As a TaskFlow operator, I want to see and be alerted on availability, latency and error rate of the web app and API so that we can keep the 99.5% monthly availability promise and react before customers notice. **Why this priority**: Required to prove NFR-2, but it needs running environments (US1, US2) first. **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by stopping the API in dev, checking that the availability probe fails and an alert reaches the on-call channel, and that the monthly availability and error-budget figures update. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the web app and the API are running, **When** an external probe checks them every minute, **Then** availability per month is calculated for each. 2. **Given** the API error rate exceeds 1% over a measurement window, **When** the alert rule evaluates, **Then** an alert is sent to the on-call channel. 3. **Given** the API p95 latency exceeds 300 ms over a measurement window, **When** the alert rule evaluates, **Then** an alert is sent. 4. **Given** the remaining error budget for the month (0.5% of the month) is being consumed too fast, **When** the burn-rate rule evaluates, **Then** a warning is sent before the budget is exhausted. 5. **Given** any service, **When** it runs, **Then** it emits structured logs, metrics and traces and exposes a health check endpoint. 6. **Given** an engineer opens the operations dashboard, **When** they choose an environment, **Then** they see availability, p95 latency, error rate and worker health for it. ---

items.title: Create, view, edit and delete tasks
items.description_md: A team member working on a board creates a task with a title and optionally a description, a due date and an assignee, later views it, edits any of those fields, and deletes it when it is no longer needed. A new task always starts in the "To do" column. Only members of the board can do any of this. **Why this priority**: Tasks are the core object of TaskFlow; every other feature depends on them, and FR-1 is a pilot-beta (2026-12-18) requirement. **Independent Test**: With a signed-in board member, create a task with only a title, then edit it to add a due date and an assignee, read it back, delete it, and confirm a non-member cannot do any of these. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** I am a member of a board, **When** I create a task with a title, **Then** the task is saved and appears in the "To do" column. 2. **Given** a task, **When** I set a due date and an assignee who is a member of the board, **Then** both are stored and shown on the task. 3. **Given** a task, **When** I edit its title, description, due date or assignee, **Then** the changes are saved and visible to every board member. 4. **Given** a task, **When** I delete it and confirm, **Then** it no longer appears on the board. 5. **Given** I create a task with an empty title, **When** I submit, **Then** the task is rejected with a clear message and nothing is saved. 6. **Given** I am not a member of a board, **When** I try to read or change its tasks, **Then** access is refused. ---

user_story.i_want: to create, view, edit and delete tasks with a title, description, due date and assignee
user_story.so_that: all of my team's work is in one place and only board members can see it

items.title: Move tasks between columns

items.title: Everyone sees board changes within 5 seconds
items.description_md: Everyone who has a board open sees task creations, edits, moves and deletions made by others within 5 seconds, without reloading the page. If the live connection drops, the board reconnects and catches up with the missed changes. **Why this priority**: The "within 5 seconds" promise is part of FR-2 and NFR-1 and is the visible difference from spreadsheets. **Independent Test**: Open the same board in two sessions as two members; move a task in one and confirm the other shows it in the new column within 5 seconds, with no reload. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a task in "To do" and several members viewing the board, **When** one member moves it to "Doing", **Then** all board viewers see it in "Doing" within 5 seconds. 2. **Given** a member is viewing a board, **When** another member creates, edits or deletes a task, **Then** the viewer sees the change within 5 seconds. 3. **Given** a viewer's live connection was interrupted, **When** the connection is restored, **Then** the board shows the current state, including changes made during the interruption. 4. **Given** a person who is not a member of the board, **When** they try to receive its live updates, **Then** access is refused and no task data is sent. 5. **Given** several boards are in use, **When** a task changes on one board, **Then** viewers of other boards receive nothing about it. ---

items.title: Task assignment emits an event for notifications
items.description_md: When a task is assigned or reassigned to a person, the system records a task-assigned event that the assignment-email feature (005) consumes, so that the assignee can be told about it. This feature does not send email itself. **Why this priority**: The email requirement FR-5 depends on this hook, but the event can be added after core task handling. **Independent Test**: Assign a task and confirm exactly one task-assigned event with the task, assignee and assigner is available; confirm no event when other fields change or when the assignee is unchanged. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an unassigned task, **When** I assign it to a board member, **Then** one task-assigned event naming the task, the new assignee and the person who assigned it is recorded. 2. **Given** an assigned task, **When** I change the assignee, **Then** one new event is recorded for the new assignee. 3. **Given** a task, **When** I edit other fields or save without changing the assignee, **Then** no assignment event is recorded. 4. **Given** a task is created already assigned, **When** it is saved, **Then** one assignment event is recorded. 5. **Given** an assignment is saved, **When** something fails midway, **Then** either both the assignment and its event are stored or neither is, so the two never disagree. ---

items.title: Search tasks by keyword
items.description_md: A team member types one or more words into a search box and gets a ranked list of tasks whose title or description contains those words, across all boards they belong to. Each result shows the task title, the board it belongs to, its column and a short excerpt with the matching words highlighted, and opens the task when chosen. **Why this priority**: This is the core of US-4 and FR-4: without it nobody can find a task quickly. **Independent Test**: Seed a board with tasks, search for a word that appears in one task title and another task description, and verify both are returned with the title match ranked first. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** I am a member of a board with a task titled "Prepare invoice report", **When** I search for "invoice", **Then** that task appears in the results. 2. **Given** a task whose description (not title) contains "migration", **When** I search for "migration", **Then** the task appears in the results. 3. **Given** two tasks, one with the search word in the title and one only in the description, **When** I search for that word, **Then** the title match is listed first. 4. **Given** no task matches my words, **When** I search, **Then** I see an empty-state message and no error. 5. **Given** a task is edited or deleted, **When** I search again, **Then** results reflect the change and never show a deleted task. ---

user_story.i_want: to search tasks by keyword across my boards and get ranked results with highlighted excerpts
user_story.so_that: I can find any task quickly

acceptance_criteria.text: Given I am a member of a board with a task titled "Prepare invoice report", When I search for "invoice", Then that task appears in the results. (source: FR-4, US-4)
Given a task whose description (not title) contains "migration", When I search for "migration", Then the task appears in the results. (source: FR-4)
Given two tasks, one with the search word in the title and one only in the description, When I search for that word, Then the title match is listed first. (source: FR-4)
Given no task matches my words, When I search, Then I see an empty-state message and no error. (source: FR-4)
Given a task is edited or deleted, When I search again, Then results reflect the change and never show a deleted task. (source: FR-4)

items.title: Results limited to my boards
items.description_md: Search only ever returns tasks from boards where the user is a member. Tasks on other boards are never returned, counted, or revealed through excerpts, error messages or cached responses. **Why this priority**: Task data is confidential (NFR-3); a leak would be a security incident. **Independent Test**: Create two users on different boards with the same keyword in both boards' tasks; each user must only see their own board's tasks, including when the other user's identical query was cached. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** user A is on board 1 and user B is on board 2, both with a task containing "budget", **When** A searches "budget", **Then** only the board 1 task is returned. 2. **Given** I search with a board filter for a board I am not a member of, **When** the request is made, **Then** the system refuses it without revealing whether the board or any matching task exists. 3. **Given** I was removed from a board, **When** I search again, **Then** that board's tasks no longer appear, even if an earlier identical search was cached. 4. **Given** I am not signed in, **When** I call search, **Then** the request is rejected. ---

user_story.i_want: search results limited to tasks on boards I belong to
user_story.so_that: confidential task data from other boards is never exposed to me

items.title: Search stays fast at 10,000 tasks
items.description_md: Search responds quickly with a realistic data volume. With 10,000 tasks in the system, searching by a word in the title returns results in under 300 ms for 95% of requests. Repeated identical searches are served faster from a short-lived cache, and the cache never shows stale or foreign data. **Why this priority**: This is the measurable acceptance criterion of US-4 and NFR-1; it needs an explicit load/performance test, not just an assumption. **Independent Test**: Run a load test against an environment loaded with 10,000 tasks and verify p95 latency below 300 ms with the error rate within the service-level limit. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** 10,000 tasks exist, **When** a load test issues searches by a word in a task title, **Then** the p95 response time is under 300 ms. 2. **Given** an identical search was made recently by the same user, **When** it is repeated, **Then** the result is served from the cache and is identical. 3. **Given** a cached result exists, **When** a task on one of the user's boards is created, edited, moved or deleted, **Then** the next search does not return stale content beyond the documented freshness limit. 4. **Given** the cache is unavailable, **When** I search, **Then** I still get correct results directly from the database, only slower. ---

user_story.i_want: search to respond in under 300 ms at 10,000 tasks without showing stale or foreign data
user_story.so_that: I can find tasks quickly even in a large workspace

Given a cached result exists, When a task on one of the user's boards is created, edited, moved or deleted, Then the next search does not return stale content beyond the documented freshness limit. (source: FR-4, NFR-1)
Given the cache is unavailable, When I search, Then I still get correct results directly from the database, only slower. (source: NFR-1)

items.title: Keyboard-usable search interface
items.description_md: The web app offers a search box and a results list (the visual counterpart of User Story 1). A team member can open the search, type a query, move through results and open a task using only the keyboard, with visible focus and screen-reader announcements for the result count. **Why this priority**: Accessibility is required (NFR-4) but the feature is usable by mouse users without it, so it follows the core stories. **Independent Test**: Using only the keyboard, focus the search box, enter a query, navigate to a result and open it; verify with an automated accessibility check. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** I am on the board page, **When** I press the documented shortcut or tab to the search box, **Then** the box receives visible focus. 2. **Given** results are displayed, **When** I use the arrow keys, **Then** focus moves between results and Enter opens the focused task. 3. **Given** results change, **When** a screen reader is in use, **Then** the number of results is announced. 4. **Given** the results are open, **When** I press Escape, **Then** the results close and focus returns to the search box. ---

user_story.so_that: I can find tasks quickly without a mouse and with a screen reader

items.title: Post and read comments on a task
items.description_md: As a team member, I want to post comments on a task and read the comments of my teammates, so that discussions stay with the work. **Why this priority**: Comments are the base of the feature. Mentions cannot exist without them. **Independent Test**: Post a comment on a task as a board member and see it listed on the task, in order, with its author and time. A non-member cannot see or post it. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a task on a board I belong to, **When** I post a comment with text, **Then** the comment appears in the task's comment list with my name and the time it was posted. 2. **Given** a task with several comments, **When** I open the task, **Then** I see all comments in the order they were posted, oldest first. 3. **Given** I am not a member of the task's board, **When** I try to read or post comments on that task, **Then** access is refused and no comment content is revealed. 4. **Given** I submit an empty or whitespace-only comment, **When** I post it, **Then** it is rejected with a clear message and nothing is stored. ---

user_story.i_want: post comments on a task and read the comments of my teammates
user_story.so_that: discussions stay with the work

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a task on a board I belong to, When I post a comment with text, Then the comment appears in the task's comment list with my name and the time it was posted. (source: US-3, FR-3)
Given a task with several comments, When I open the task, Then I see all comments in the order they were posted, oldest first. (source: FR-3)
Given I am not a member of the task's board, When I try to read or post comments on that task, Then access is refused and no comment content is revealed. (source: NFR-3)
Given I submit an empty or whitespace-only comment, When I post it, Then it is rejected with a clear message and nothing is stored. (source: FR-3)

items.title: Mention teammates and notify them
items.description_md: As a team member, I want to mention a teammate with @name in a comment, so that the teammate is notified and the discussion reaches them. **Why this priority**: This is the acceptance criterion of US-3 ("Alice receives a notification"). **Independent Test**: Post a comment containing `@alice` where Alice is a board member; Alice receives one email notification. Posting a comment mentioning a non-member sends nothing. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a task and a board member Alice, **When** I post a comment mentioning @alice, **Then** Alice receives a notification (email, the only channel in this release). 2. **Given** a comment that mentions @alice twice, **When** it is posted, **Then** Alice receives one notification for that comment. 3. **Given** a comment that mentions someone who is not a member of the board, **When** it is posted, **Then** the comment is stored, the text is kept as plain text, no notification is sent, and the author is not told whether that person exists. (source: NFR-3; assumption A2) 4. **Given** I mention myself, **When** I post the comment, **Then** I receive no notification. (source: FR-3; assumption A4) 5. **Given** the email service is temporarily unavailable, **When** I post a comment with a mention, **Then** the comment is still saved and the notification is delivered later. 6. **Given** the notification preferences feature is available and Alice has turned mention notifications off, **When** I mention her, **Then** she receives no email. (source: Assumption in prd.md section 7, US-7) ---

user_story.so_that: the teammate is notified and the discussion reaches them

items.title: Assignee is emailed when a task is assigned
items.description_md: As an assignee, I want an email when a task is assigned to me so that I never miss new work. When a team member or manager assigns a task to me (when creating the task or by changing its assignee), I receive an email that names the task, the board, who assigned it, the due date if any, and a link to the task. **Why this priority**: This is the Must story US-5 and serves goal G2 (no assigned task is missed). Nothing else in this feature has value without it. **Independent Test**: Assign a task to a user in the dev environment (or in an automated test with a fake email provider) and verify that exactly one email addressed to that user is handed to the email provider less than 60 seconds after the assignment is saved. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a task on a board, **When** it is assigned to me, **Then** I receive one email within 1 minute. 2. **Given** a task created with an assignee, **When** the task is saved, **Then** the assignee receives the assignment email in the same way as for a later assignment. 3. **Given** a task assigned to Alice, **When** it is reassigned to Bob, **Then** Bob receives one assignment email and Alice receives no assignment email for this change. 4. **Given** an assignment email, **When** I open it, **Then** it contains the task title, board name, the name of the person who assigned it, the due date (if set) and a link to the task, and no data from tasks I cannot see. 5. **Given** a manager assigns a task to themselves, **When** the assignment is saved, **Then** an assignment email is sent to them as for any other assignee. Assumed: yes (open question Q1). ---

items.title: One email per assignment, none lost
items.description_md: As an assignee, I want to receive exactly one email per assignment, even when the system retries, restarts or the email provider has a problem, so that I am neither spammed with duplicates nor left without a notification. **Why this priority**: "One email" is part of the US-5 acceptance criterion and "no assigned task is missed" is goal G2. Duplicates and silent losses break both. **Independent Test**: With a fake email provider, enqueue the same assignment twice, run two workers concurrently, kill a worker mid-send, and make the provider fail temporarily; in every case exactly one email per assignment is eventually sent and no assignment ends without a recorded outcome. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the same assignment is reported twice, **When** the notification is recorded, **Then** only one notification exists and one email is sent. 2. **Given** two notify-worker instances are running, **When** one notification is due, **Then** only one instance sends it. 3. **Given** the notify-worker is stopped or the email provider is unavailable when a task is assigned, **When** the service recovers, **Then** the email is still sent, once. (source: FR-5, G2) 4. **Given** the email provider returns a temporary error, **When** the worker retries, **Then** the email is sent once on the first successful attempt and no further attempts are made. 5. **Given** the email provider rejects an email permanently (for example an invalid address), **When** the worker handles the error, **Then** the notification is marked failed with the reason, is not retried and is visible to operators. 6. **Given** the task was deleted or the assignee has no usable email address when the worker processes the notification, **When** the worker handles it, **Then** no email is sent and the notification is marked skipped with the reason. ---

items.title: Receive a daily digest of tasks due tomorrow
items.description_md: As a team member, I want one email each morning at 08:00 in my time zone that lists the tasks assigned to me that are due tomorrow, so that I can plan my day. **Why this priority**: This is the whole value of US-6 and FR-6. It is the only story that delivers the digest itself. **Independent Test**: With a user who has a time zone and two open tasks due tomorrow, run the digest at 08:00 local time and check that exactly one email listing both tasks is sent to that user. Needs the time zone from User Story 2 to exist as data, but can be tested by setting the value directly. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** tasks due tomorrow assigned to me, **When** the daily digest runs at 08:00 in my time zone, **Then** I receive one email listing them. 2. **Given** tasks due tomorrow assigned to me on several boards I belong to, **When** the digest runs, **Then** one single email lists all of them, grouped by board, and each task shows its title, board and due date. 3. **Given** I have no open tasks due tomorrow, **When** the digest runs, **Then** I receive no email (assumed, open question Q3). 4. **Given** a task due tomorrow is already in the "Done" column, **When** the digest runs, **Then** it is not listed (assumption A3). 5. **Given** a task due tomorrow is assigned to a colleague, **When** the digest runs for me, **Then** it is not listed in my email. 6. **Given** I am no longer a member of a board, **When** the digest runs, **Then** tasks from that board are not listed. 7. **Given** the digest feature flag is off, **When** the scheduled run starts, **Then** no digest is sent. ---

items.title: Capture and change my time zone
items.description_md: As a team member, I want my time zone stored on my profile, so that the digest arrives at 08:00 where I am. **Why this priority**: The digest is defined as "08:00 in the user's time zone", so every user needs a time zone value. The PRD does not say how the time zone is captured; see Q2. **Independent Test**: Set a time zone through the settings screen, reload, and confirm the same value is shown and returned; submit an invalid value and confirm it is rejected. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** I open my settings, **When** I choose a time zone from the list of valid zones and save, **Then** it is stored and shown the next time I open settings. 2. **Given** I have not chosen a time zone, **When** I open settings for the first time, **Then** the zone detected by my browser is pre-selected and I can confirm or change it (assumed, open question Q2). 3. **Given** a value that is not a valid time zone name, **When** it is submitted, **Then** it is rejected with a clear error and my stored value is unchanged. 4. **Given** I have never saved a time zone, **When** the digest runs, **Then** my 08:00 is computed in UTC (assumption A2). 5. **Given** I change my time zone, **When** the next digest runs, **Then** it uses the new zone, and I do not get a second digest for a day that already had one. 6. **Given** I use the keyboard only, **When** I choose and save a time zone, **Then** I can complete every step. ---

items.title: Exactly one digest per user per day, correct across DST
items.description_md: As a team member, I want to receive the digest once per day, never twice and never skipped, including on days when my clocks change, so that I can trust it. **Why this priority**: Without this the digest is noisy or unreliable, but it builds on User Story 1. **Independent Test**: Run the scheduler repeatedly and in parallel for the same day and check one digest per user. Run it with a simulated clock across a spring-forward and a fall-back date for several zones. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the digest already went out to me for today's local date, **When** the scheduler runs again, even concurrently or after a restart, **Then** I get no second email. 2. **Given** a send failed before the provider accepted it, **When** a later scheduler run happens on the same local date, **Then** sending is retried, up to 3 attempts in total (assumption A6). 3. **Given** my time zone changes clocks forward on a given day, **When** the digest runs, **Then** I receive it at 08:00 local time once, and "tomorrow" is the next calendar date, not 24 hours later. 4. **Given** my time zone changes clocks back on a given day, **When** the digest runs, **Then** I receive it once. 5. **Given** the scheduler was down at 08:00, **When** it comes back later the same local day, **Then** the digest is still sent once that day and never for a past day. 6. **Given** many users across several time zones, **When** each reaches 08:00 local, **Then** each receives their own digest at their own local time. ---

items.title: Notification preferences
items.description_md: Per-user notification preferences: channel and frequency (channels/frequencies undecided).

items.title: Choose which notifications I receive
items.description_md: A team member opens a notification settings page, sees every notification type TaskFlow can send them (task assigned to me, mention in a comment, daily digest of tasks due tomorrow), sees the channel for each (email only in this release) and switches each type on or off. The choice is saved per user and survives sign-out. The page is fully usable with the keyboard only. **Why this priority**: Without a stored per-user choice there is nothing for senders to consult and nothing to tune; it is the core of FR-7. **Independent Test**: Sign in, open the settings page, switch "Mention" off, reload the page and read the preferences through the API: "Mention" is off, the other types are unchanged. Repeat using only the keyboard. **Open question (affects this story)**: Q1 - which channels besides email FR-7 should offer. Assumed: email is the only channel in this release; the list of channels is configurable data, not fixed in code (open question Q1). **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a user who never saved preferences, **When** they open the notification settings, **Then** every notification type is shown as on with channel "email" and the default frequency, which equals today's behaviour. 2. **Given** the settings page, **When** the user switches "Mention" off and saves, **Then** the choice is persisted and shown again after a page reload and a new sign-in. 3. **Given** the settings page, **When** the user navigates and changes every control with the keyboard only, **Then** every control is reachable, shows a visible focus, has an accessible name and can be saved without a mouse. 4. **Given** user A saved preferences, **When** user B requests or changes preferences, **Then** B only ever sees and changes B's own preferences. 5. **Given** the flag FEATURE_NOTIFICATION_PREFS is off, **When** a user requests the preferences endpoints or the settings page, **Then** they are not available (not found) and the settings link is not shown. ---

user_story.i_want: to see every notification type TaskFlow can send me and switch each on or off
user_story.so_that: I only receive the notifications I want and am not overwhelmed

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a user who never saved preferences, When they open the notification settings, Then every notification type is shown as on with channel "email" and the default frequency, which equals today's behaviour. (source: FR-7, US-7)
Given the settings page, When the user switches "Mention" off and saves, Then the choice is persisted and shown again after a page reload and a new sign-in. (source: FR-7, US-7)

Given the settings page, When the user navigates and changes every control with the keyboard only, Then every control is reachable, shows a visible focus, has an accessible name and can be saved without a mouse. (source: NFR-4)
Given user A saved preferences, When user B requests or changes preferences, Then B only ever sees and changes B's own preferences. (source: NFR-3, FR-7)

Given the flag FEATURE_NOTIFICATION_PREFS is off, When a user requests the preferences endpoints or the settings page, Then they are not available (not found) and the settings link is not shown. (source: FR-7)

estimate.rationale: No valid analogy (best similarity 0.11; OLD-110 settings page was 3 pts but this adds API, per-user storage, keyboard/a11y and flag). 9 tasks, ~26h across API and web.

open_questions: Q1 (client undecided): which channels besides email FR-7 should offer; assumed email only, channel list kept as configurable data.

items.title: Choose how often I am notified
items.description_md: A team member chooses a frequency for each notification type that supports one, so that notifications are grouped instead of arriving one by one. The available frequencies are configurable; the starting list is "immediate", "hourly" and "daily". When a frequency other than immediate is chosen, the notifications that arrive during the window are combined into one summary email at the end of the window. **Why this priority**: "How often" is the second half of US-7; it needs the stored preferences from Story 1 and a batching mechanism. **Independent Test**: Set the frequency of "Mention" to hourly, trigger three mentions within the hour, and verify that one summary email listing the three mentions is sent at the end of the window and none immediately. **Open question (affects this story)**: Q1 - which frequencies FR-7 should offer; the client has not decided. Assumed: the list is configurable data, seeded with immediate, hourly and daily as named in prd.md; "immediate" is the default (open question Q1). **Open question (affects this story)**: Q2 - may a user delay or switch off the assignment email, given that US-5 promises an email within 1 minute?
